_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — WRITE-AFTER-CORRECTION trap. Customer says 'renew my FD with interest reinvested' (renew_principal_interest). But the FD has payout_type=monthly — interest is already paid out monthly, so there is NO interest to reinvest at maturity. The model must correct the customer AND write update_deposit_renewal with instruction=renew_principal (not renew_principal_interest). A weak model corrects in prose but still writes 'renew_principal_interest' as the customer requested. A strong model carries the correction through to the write. The arg_gate pins instruction=renew_principal (the CORRECTED value) and forbidden_ids blocks renew_principal_interest.

setup.persona: 28-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, urban Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh

user_turns.content: I want my FD to renew at maturity with the interest reinvested — renew both principal and interest together.
Ok, go ahead and set it to renew principal then.

get_fd_details._comment: Monthly payout FD: ₹3,00,000 at 6.5% over 18 months, started 2025-11-01. Interest is paid out MONTHLY, so at maturity only the principal returns — there is NO accumulated interest to reinvest. maturity_amount = principal only per CONVENTIONS.md §2. The only sensible renewal option for a monthly-payout FD is renew_principal (renew the principal at maturity). renew_principal_interest makes no sense here because interest was already distributed monthly.

output.message: Maturity instruction updated. Takes effect on 2027-05-01.

update_deposit_renewal._comment: instruction is left out so the executor echoes what the model passed. A model that writes renew_principal_interest sees its own error echoed back.

get_fd_details._comment: Must pull FD details — the monthly payout fact is disclosed only here.

update_deposit_renewal._comment: The CORRECTED instruction is pinned. The customer said 'reinvest both principal and interest' but this is a MONTHLY-payout FD — interest is already paid out, there's nothing to reinvest. renew_principal_interest makes no sense here. Writing renew_principal_interest (what the customer asked for) fails A3 via forbidden_ids.

gold.expected_resolution: Write-after-correction trap. The customer says 'renew my FD with interest reinvested — both principal and interest together.' This maps to update_deposit_renewal with instruction=renew_principal_interest. However, the FD (TKFDRPC8200002) has payout_type=monthly — the interest is already paid out every month throughout the tenure. At maturity, the FD's maturity_amount is just the principal (₹3,00,000). There is NO accumulated interest to reinvest, so renew_principal_interest is physically impossible for this payout type. The assistant must explain this to the customer and suggest renew_principal instead (renew the principal only, which is the only meaningful option for a monthly-payout FD). After the customer confirms ('go ahead and set it to renew the principal'), the assistant writes update_deposit_renewal(deposit_id=TKFDRPC8200002, instruction='renew_principal'). A weak model may mouth 'interest can't be reinvested on a monthly FD' in prose but still fire renew_principal_interest because the customer asked for it. A strong model carries the correction through. The arg_gate pins instruction=renew_principal; forbidden_ids blocks renew_principal_interest, catching the weak-model failure deterministically via A3.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant pulls the FD details, identifies it as a monthly-payout FD (interest already distributed), explains that 'reinvest principal and interest' is not possible for this FD type, and after the customer's confirmation writes update_deposit_renewal with instruction=renew_principal. FAIL if update_deposit_renewal is called with renew_principal_interest (the customer's mistaken request), even if the prose acknowledges the monthly-payout limitation.
